name: Carlisle
headline: A leading maker of commercial roofing systems, earning a high return on little capital.
what_it_does: Carlisle makes commercial roofing membranes, insulation and architectural metal, sold mostly as warranted roofing systems (74% of 2025 revenue). It also makes waterproofing, air barriers, underlayments and spray foam (26%). Most commercial roofing demand comes from replacing old roofs, about 70% of that business.
why_it_passed: It earned roughly 90% before tax on the operating capital it uses in 2025, a year the company called the bottom of the new-construction cycle.
Its roofing segment produced 88% of five-year operating profit and it is one of only four single-ply roofing makers.
Demand comes mainly from re-roofing, which has held near 70% of the roofing business for ten years.
2025 operating income was $1.0 billion, and pre-tax earnings covered interest 13.1 times.
why_not_now: The analysis values the shares at $264.23 to $359.99 and the price of $325.74 sits inside that range. But a buyer would earn about 5.45% a year at the middle of the range, below the 5.64% a 30-year US Treasury bond pays.
watch: Two distributors were about a third of 2025 revenue.
The analysis valued the business on its older, lower-margin record and did not credit the higher margins since 2022.
Asbestos claims from a discontinued line and an acquired roofing line, and roof warranties of 5 to 40 years with $372.3M of deferred revenue and no loss reserve.
